Wolborz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wolbórz, Poland

Demolished. Until the 18th century, Wolbórz's Jews were barred from settling under the De Non-Tolerandis Iudaeis privilege and lived instead in the neighboring village of Wesoła; after the privilege's 1807 abolition, the town's Jewish population grew, and in the 1830s the Hasidic tzadik Rabbi Issachar Dow Ber ha-Kohen Tornheim settled there and established his own court, complete with an orchestra and choir. When an independent kehilla was founded in 1862, Tornheim became its rabbi. In October 1942, the Germans deported over 400 Jews to the Piotrków Trybunalski Ghetto and then to Treblinka; only 20 survived the war. This cemetery was likely established in 1862, alongside the new kehilla.
